Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No. 0249/2017 registered at Police Station Govindpuri, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Ms. Naina Walia and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Vivek Tomar, Police Station Govindpuri, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 25.10.2015 and no child was born out of the said wedlock.
Thereafter, due to temperamental differences that arose between the parties, they started living separately from each other since 29.03.2016.

On the basis of complaint filed by respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing No.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 by way of mutual consent vide decree sheet dated 14.05.2019 dissolved their marriage.

During the pendency of the present FIR, with the intervention of family members and respectable person of the society, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes before Counselling Cell, Saket Court, New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 15,03.2018.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Saket Court, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Counselling Cell, Saket Court, New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 15,03.2018.
8.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Saket Court, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

9. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 2,50,000/- in four instalments in the following manner:
a. First instalment of Rs.75,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the first motion petition. b. Second instalment of Rs.75,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the second motion petition.

c.
Third instalment of Rs.50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of withdrawing petition filed under Section 125 Cr.P.C. d. Fourth/Final instalment of Rs.50,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

10. The complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs.50,000/- today, i.e., 15.02.2023 by way of DD bearing No. 025553 for a sum of Rs.
50,000/- drawn on The Kangra Co- operative Bank Limited and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.

It would thus be in interest of justice,
to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 0249/2017 registered at Police Station Govindpuri, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
